meta.spec_reference: Microsoft RIFF / WAVE specification: 'Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0' (Microsoft Corporation, 1994), sections 'RIFF File Format', 'WAVE File Format' and 'Waveform Data Chunk'; wFormatTag registry from the Microsoft Windows Multimedia API header mmreg.h; Microsoft IMA/DVI ADPCM block layout as used by WAVE_FORMAT_DVIADPCM (0x0011); WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE from Microsoft 'Multiple Channel Audio Data and WAVE Files' (2007); sampler (smpl) and cue chunk layout from the same 1994 document; RF64/EBU Tech 3306 noted but out of scope; secondary reference cited by the template itself at line 17 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WAV).

schema_extensions.name: meta.filename_model_label
schema_extensions.why: The output filename supplied by the task harness carries the label 'qwen3.8-max'. meta.model records the model that actually produced this extraction; the harness label is preserved separately so the comparison pipeline can still recover it without falsifying provenance.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead_bound
schema_extensions.why: The schema's 'lookahead' key requires a 'values' set, but the template has two ReadUInt( FTell()+4 ) calls (lines 166 and 566) that read a forthcoming chunkSize purely as a bounds check, not as a value-set lookup. lookahead_bound records the call site, its purpose and what happens to the parse when the value is wrong, which is the information the rewrite step needs.

schema_extensions.name: condition
schema_extensions.why: DATACHUNK.waveformData and FORMATCHUNK.unknown are well-formed only under a specific wFormatTag. The condition names the format-tag value that activates the requirement, so the rewrite step does not emit ADPCM framing into a PCM file.

schema_extensions.name: derivation
schema_extensions.why: Some fields listed in payload_wellformedness.derives_from are themselves derived (wBlockAlign, wSamplesPerBlock, dwAvgBytesPerSec). For those, 'must_remain_unconstrained: true' means 'never pinned to a constant to suit a fixed payload', not 'emit arbitrary values'; derivation states the formula whose inputs carry the diversity.

schema_extensions.name: predicate
schema_extensions.why: The RIFF even-byte alignment rule activates on the parity of a chunk size, which is not expressible with equals/in/min/max/present/absent. predicate carries the literal template expression, e.g. '(chunkSize & 1) == 1'.

schema_extensions.name: forbidden_values
schema_extensions.why: Used for the single case where a Tier C field's value makes a derived Tier A field illegal (wChannels == 0 forces wBlockAlign == 0, which the template rejects at line 78). It states the rule on the derived field instead of placing a numeric bound on the free field.

schema_extensions.name: weighting_note
schema_extensions.where: constraints.<field> (Tier B entries with an open legal namespace)
schema_extensions.why: wFormatTag, LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID and SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer have legal sets that are finite but open-ended in practice. The full legal set is recorded as required, and weighting_note tells the rewrite step how to sample it so the deep-parsing preferred values still dominate.

meta.structure_note: A WAV file is a little-endian RIFF envelope: a 12-byte 'RIFF'+size+'WAVE' head followed by an unordered sequence of 8-byte-header chunks running to end of file, where 'fmt ' and 'data' are mandatory and 'fact', 'cue ', 'smpl', 'LIST' and unknown FOURCC chunks are optional; every chunk carries its own payload length and every odd-length chunk payload is followed by one alignment pad byte. The format has no terminator chunk and no CRC anywhere. Encoded/compressed payloads exist only inside the 'data' chunk when wFormatTag selects a compressed codec (Microsoft ADPCM 0x0002, DVI/IMA ADPCM 0x0011, MPEG 0x0050/0x0055, GSM 0x0031, etc.); for the common PCM (0x0001) and IEEE float (0x0003) tags the data payload is raw little-endian samples with no framing at all, so its only well-formedness requirement is exact size agreement with chunkSize and wBlockAlign. Depth here is bought by chunk-length consistency and format-tag/sample-shape agreement, not by a codec envelope.

WAVRIFFHEADER.groupID.tier_rationale: The template hard-stops at lines 523-527 with Warning( "File is not a valid wave file. Template stopped." ) followed by return -1 when this is not 'RIFF', and every real decoder (ffmpeg riff.c, libsndfile wav_read_header, SoX) refuses the file before reading a single chunk.
WAVRIFFHEADER.groupID.description: The RIFF form identifier at file offset 0, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'RIFF'.
WAVRIFFHEADER.groupID.notes: Corroborated by the template's own ID Bytes comment at line 10: '//  ID Bytes: 52 49 46 46 [+4] 57 41 56 45 //RIFF????WAVE'. Written as four ASCII bytes in file order, not as an integer; the [+4] gap in that pattern is the hsize field.

WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.tier_rationale: ffmpeg's WAV demuxer derives riff_end from this field and stops scanning chunks there, so an under-declared hsize makes the demuxer abandon the file before it ever reaches the 'data' chunk; libsndfile warns and truncates on a RIFF length mismatch. Pinning it costs no diversity because it is computed from the bytes actually emitted.
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.description: The RIFF form length: the number of bytes that follow this field to the end of the file, i.e. FileSize() - 8.
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.algorithm: byte count: FileSize() - 8, equivalently 4 bytes of riffType plus the sum over every top-level chunk of (8-byte header + chunkSize payload + odd-alignment pad byte)
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.covers: riffType[4] and the entire top-level chunk sequence emitted by the while( !FEof() ) loop at lines 532-573, including each chunk's 8-byte header, its chunkSize payload bytes and its optional pad byte
WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.notes: Declared 'long' but read little-endian per LittleEndian() at line 518 and semantically an unsigned 32-bit RIFF size. Compute it last, after all chunk bytes exist - never guess it. A value of 0xFFFFFFFF switches the file to RF64 semantics where the true length lives in a 'ds64' chunk; that is out of scope and should not be emitted.

WAVRIFFHEADER.riffType.tier_rationale: The same hard gate at lines 523-527 stops the template with 'File is not a valid wave file' when this is not 'WAVE'; ffmpeg and libsndfile check the RIFF form type identically and refuse the file before any chunk is parsed.
WAVRIFFHEADER.riffType.description: The RIFF form type at file offset 8, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'WAVE' for this container to be a wave file.
WAVRIFFHEADER.riffType.notes: 'WAVE' is the only form type this template accepts. Sibling RIFF forms such as 'AVI ' and 'RMID' exist in the RIFF family but are not WAV and must not be emitted here.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The chunk-dispatch switch at lines 538-572 only instantiates FORMATCHUNK when the four tag bytes read at line 535 equal 'fmt '; any other value takes a different branch, so haveValidFormat stays false (line 21) and the following 'data' chunk is rejected at lines 70-74.
FORMATCHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying the format chunk, which must be 'fmt ' - note the trailing space, four bytes exactly.
FORMATCHUNK.chunkID.notes: The lookahead is ReadBytes( tag, FTell(), 4 ) at line 535 feeding switch( tag ) at line 538; the six compared literals are the complete recognised set and every other FOURCC falls to the default UNKNOWNCHUNK branch at lines 564-571. The trailing space in 'fmt ' is the classic place to get this wrong: 0x66 0x6d 0x74 0x20.

FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: The template uses this value to size the unknown[] filler at lines 55-56 and to decide the odd-alignment pad at line 59, so a wrong value desynchronises every subsequent chunk boundary and the remainder of the file parses as garbage; ffmpeg and libsndfile walk chunks by declared size and misread or refuse the file the same way.
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the format chunk's payload, excluding its own 8-byte header and excluding the optional pad byte.
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: 16 for a plain WAVEFORMATEX (wFormatTag..wBitsPerSample), 18 when wcbsize plus wSamplesPerBlock follow (wFormatTag 2 or 17), 40 for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (0xFFFE), or 18 + cbSize for any codec carrying extra format bytes
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: every byte from wFormatTag through wBitsPerSample plus, when present, wcbsize, wSamplesPerBlock and the unknown[] run at line 56 - exactly the span the template measures as (FTell() - pos) with pos captured at line 38
FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: The template's own consistency expression is line 55: if( chunkSize > (FTell() - pos) ) uchar unknown[ chunkSize - (FTell() - pos) ]; Satisfy it by construction - emit the format payload first, then write its measured length here. libsndfile rejects an undersized fmt chunk (SFE_WAV_FMT_SHORT) and ffmpeg bails on a chunk that overruns the RIFF end.

FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.tier_rationale: This is a finite enumeration of registered codec identifiers, not a single pinned value: the template compares it against the literal 17 at line 45 to decide whether two extra fields follow, and every decoder has a distinct branch per tag, so each legal value is real coverage that must not be dropped.
FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.description: The codec identifier that selects how the 'data' chunk payload is interpreted and which extra format fields follow.
FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.completeness_reason: The wFormatTag namespace is an open 16-bit registry: mmreg.h registers several hundred tags and any unregistered 16-bit value is still a syntactically legal WAV field that a conforming reader must simply report as an unsupported codec. The list above is exhaustive over the tags a WAVE decoder actually branches on (1 PCM, 2 MS ADPCM, 3 IEEE float, 6 A-law, 7 mu-law, 17 IMA ADPCM, 80/85 MPEG, 353-356 WMA, 5632-5634 AAC, 31265/31266 AMR, 65534 EXTENSIBLE) plus the historically significant ACM-registered tags; it omits only obscure vendor tags whose registered names I cannot verify. The omission is a knowledge limit, never a productivity judgement - the generator should treat all 65536 possible values as legal.
FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.weighting_note: Weight the preferred values on the great majority of generated files: 1 (PCM) and 3 (IEEE float) reach the full sample-decoding pipeline; 2 and 17 reach the ADPCM block decoders and are the only tags for which this template reads the extra wcbsize/wSamplesPerBlock fields; 6 and 7 reach the G.711 companding tables; 65534 (EXTENSIBLE) reaches the WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE/GUID branch. Sample the remaining legal tags occasionally - each one is a distinct 'unsupported codec' path that the decoder executes and therefore real coverage.
FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.notes: Line 45 is the only literal comparison against wFormatTag in the template and it is decisive: tag 17 (DVI/IMA ADPCM) is the one case where the template reads two additional fields (wcbsize at line 47, wSamplesPerBlock at line 48), so every other tag yields a 16-byte fmt payload unless extra bytes are supplied through FORMATCHUNK.unknown. Declared 'short' (signed) but semantically an unsigned 16-bit registry value - 65534 and 65535 must be written as the unsigned bit patterns 0xFFFE and 0xFFFF.

FORMATCHUNK.wChannels.tier_rationale: A wrong channel count still yields a file every decoder will process - it only changes how many interleaved samples are read per block - and it is the single largest driver of distinct decoder paths (mono fast paths, stereo interleaving, multichannel matrixing), so bounding it would sell diversity for nothing.
FORMATCHUNK.wChannels.description: Number of interleaved audio channels declared for the stream; any positive value is a legal channel count and the sample arrays and wBlockAlign are derived from it.
FORMATCHUNK.wChannels.notes: Deliberately left with no minimum, no maximum and no value set. Do NOT narrow this field to make a fixed sample payload fit - the payload must be derived from it (see DATACHUNK.samples / DATACHUNK.waveformData derives_from). The template consumes it directly as an array length at lines 103/105/107 and as a branch selector at lines 83, 88 and 93. The one format-derived exception is recorded as a dependency, not here: wChannels == 0 forces wBlockAlign == 0, which line 78 rejects.

FORMATCHUNK.dwSamplesPerSec.tier_rationale: Sample rate is never validated by a conforming decoder - it only sets playback pitch and duration arithmetic - so every value produces a file that is fully parsed; pinning it to a set of 'standard' rates would collapse one of the cheapest sources of file-to-file difference.
FORMATCHUNK.dwSamplesPerSec.description: Sampling frequency in hertz used to interpret and time the sample data.
FORMATCHUNK.dwSamplesPerSec.notes: No 'common rates' list is given on purpose. It feeds dwAvgBytesPerSec (see that entry's depends_on) and SMPLCHUNK.Sample_Period by convention only; deriving those from this field keeps the file self-consistent while this field itself stays completely free.

FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.tier_rationale: This is a derived consistency field rather than a free one: ffmpeg's wav demuxer falls back to 8*dwAvgBytesPerSec for the stream bit rate and duration when no other source exists, and for compressed codecs the ACM layer sizes its conversion buffers from it, so an inconsistent value corrupts duration/seek arithmetic downstream. It costs zero diversity because it is computed from fields that stay completely free.
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.description: Average number of bytes per second of stream data, which for all the codecs a WAV decoder implements equals dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign.
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.algorithm: dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign (equivalently dwSamplesPerSec * wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 for PCM); the template never checks it, so this comes from the RIFF/WAVE specification
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.covers: no byte span - it is a rate derived from other fmt fields, not a length of anything in the file
FORMATCHUNK.dwAvgBytesPerSec.notes: Recorded as Tier A only in the sense that it must be derived, never random: its two inputs (dwSamplesPerSec, wChannels, wBitsPerSample) are free, so deriving this field adds file-to-file variety rather than removing it. Never pin it to a constant such as 176400 - that is exactly the anti-pattern this extraction exists to prevent.

FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.tier_rationale: The template refuses to parse any samples when this is zero or when chunkSize is not an exact multiple of it (line 78), falling back to an opaque byte blob; real decoders do worse - ffmpeg and libsndfile derive the interleaved frame size from it and reject or truncate the stream when it disagrees with wChannels * wBitsPerSample.
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.description: Block alignment in bytes: the number of bytes occupied by one interleaved frame of all channels, which for uncompressed formats is wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8.
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.algorithm: PCM / IEEE float / A-law / mu-law: wChannels * (wBitsPerSample / 8), rounded up to a whole byte. Microsoft ADPCM (tag 2): the chosen block size in bytes. DVI/IMA ADPCM (tag 17): the chosen block size in bytes, from which wSamplesPerBlock is then derived. MPEG-in-WAV (tags 80/85): the MPEG frame size.
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.covers: no byte span - it is the stride used to slice the data chunk payload; DATACHUNK.chunkSize must be an exact multiple of it
FORMATCHUNK.wBlockAlign.notes: Line 78 also shows this field is used as a divisor (chunkSize % (int)format.wBlockAlign), so it must be non-zero. It is derived from wChannels and wBitsPerSample, both of which remain free - derive it, never hard-code it, and never shrink wChannels to make a hard-coded block align work.

FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.tier_rationale: The template itself compares this against the literals 8, 16 and 32 at lines 77, 102, 104 and 106 to choose the sample element type, and a value no codec defines makes libsndfile and ffmpeg refuse the stream - so it is a finite enumeration whose members are each a separate decoder branch, not a free dimension.
FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.description: Number of bits used to store one sample of one channel; the legal set depends on wFormatTag and each member selects a different sample element width in the data chunk.
value_names: 4-bit (Microsoft ADPCM tag 2 and DVI/IMA ADPCM tag 17)
24-bit PCM signed, packed 3 bytes per sample
FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.completeness_reason: This is the complete set used by every codec a WAVE decoder actually implements, but the field is nominally codec-defined: an arbitrary compressed codec may declare other widths (3-bit, 5-bit, VBR). The six values listed are exhaustive over tags 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 and 17, which are the tags with real decoder branches.
FORMATCHUNK.wBitsPerSample.notes: Line 77 is a three-way literal comparison (8, 16, 32) that decides between the typed sample arrays and the opaque waveformData[] fallback; 24 and 64 are deliberately included even though this template routes them to the fallback, because libsndfile and ffmpeg both implement them and 24-bit packed and 64-bit float are separate decode paths. The per-tag legal subsets are recorded in dependencies.

FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.tier_rationale: This is the cbSize byte count that tells the decoder how many extra format bytes follow; ffmpeg copies exactly cbSize bytes into the codec extradata and libsndfile validates the fmt chunk length against it, so a wrong value truncates the codec setup or desynchronises the chunk stream.
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.description: Size in bytes of the codec-specific format information that follows the 16-byte WAVEFORMATEX core, present in this template only for wFormatTag 17.
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.algorithm: byte count of the extra format data that follows this field: 2 for DVI/IMA ADPCM (tag 17, the wSamplesPerBlock word only), 32 for Microsoft ADPCM (tag 2: 2-byte coefficient count plus 30 bytes of coefficient pairs), 22 for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (tag 65534: validBitsPerSample + channelMask + SubFormat GUID)
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.covers: every byte from wSamplesPerBlock (or the equivalent extra data) to the end of the format chunk payload, i.e. the FORMATCHUNK.unknown[] run when the codec uses one
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.condition: present only when wFormatTag is 2, 17 or 65534 (the template instantiates it for tag 17 at line 45)
FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize.notes: Must satisfy FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize == 18 + wcbsize for the tags that carry it. When the field is absent (plain PCM or IEEE float) the fmt chunk is exactly 16 bytes.

FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.tier_rationale: For DVI/IMA ADPCM the decoder reads this from the extradata and uses it as the sample count per ADPCM block; ffmpeg's adpcm_ima_wav decoder sizes each frame from it, so a value that disagrees with wBlockAlign makes every block decode to the wrong length and the stream is dropped. It is derived, so pinning the formula costs no diversity.
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.description: Number of decoded samples produced by one ADPCM block per channel, derived from the block alignment and channel count.
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.algorithm: DVI/IMA ADPCM (tag 17): wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign - 4 * wChannels) * 2 / wChannels + 1. Microsoft ADPCM (tag 2): wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign / wChannels - 7) * 2 + 2, with the coefficient set supplied in the extra format bytes.
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.covers: no byte span - it is the decode-loop bound for one ADPCM block inside the data chunk payload
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.condition: present only when wFormatTag is 2 or 17 (instantiated for tag 17 at line 45-49)
FORMATCHUNK.wSamplesPerBlock.notes: This is the field where the GIF mistake would be made: the correct direction is to choose a free wBlockAlign and wChannels, then compute wSamplesPerBlock and emit that many samples per ADPCM block. Never pick a fixed wSamplesPerBlock and then bend wBlockAlign or wChannels to match it.

FORMATCHUNK.unknown.tier_rationale: The template reads this run purely to consume leftover bytes (lines 55-56) and never inspects a single byte of it; its contents are free, and inventing a value set here would remove the only place extra codec bytes can vary.
FORMATCHUNK.unknown.description: Trailing bytes of the format chunk beyond the fields the template knows, sized by chunkSize minus what has already been consumed.
FORMATCHUNK.unknown.notes: Contents are unconstrained, but its LENGTH is not a free choice: it is exactly chunkSize - (bytes already emitted in this chunk), which is what lines 55-56 compute. The one format-mandated exception is recorded as a dependency: when wFormatTag == 65534 this run must hold the 22-byte WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE tail (cbSize 22, validBitsPerSample, channelMask, 16-byte SubFormat GUID).

FORMATCHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: The pad byte exists only to restore even alignment; no reader inspects its value (ffmpeg and libsndfile both skip it unconditionally), so it is exactly the 'padding whose value is unchecked' case and constraining it would add nothing.
FORMATCHUNK.padding.description: Single RIFF alignment byte emitted after a chunk whose payload length is odd.
FORMATCHUNK.padding.notes: Its PRESENCE and COUNT are a hard structural rule (see dependencies and structure): emit exactly one pad byte when chunkSize is odd and none when it is even, and count that byte in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize but never in chunkSize. Its VALUE is free; 0x00 is conventional.

DATACHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The dispatch switch at lines 544-547 instantiates DATACHUNK only when the four tag bytes read at line 535 are 'data'; any other value routes the bytes to a different struct, so the audio payload is never parsed at all.
DATACHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying the waveform data chunk, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'data'.
DATACHUNK.chunkID.notes: No trailing space here - unlike 'fmt ' and 'cue '. Decoders that support the RF64 variant also accept 'rdat' with the true size carried in a 'ds64' chunk; that is out of scope for this template.

DATACHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: The template gates the entire sample-parsing block on this value - line 78 refuses typed samples unless chunkSize % wBlockAlign == 0, and lines 86/91/96/108 use it as the array length - and real decoders read exactly chunkSize bytes as audio, so a value that disagrees with the bytes actually present either truncates the audio or lets the next chunk be parsed from the middle of a sample.
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the sample payload that immediately follows, excluding the 8-byte chunk header and the optional pad byte.
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count of the emitted sample payload, rounded to a whole number of blocks: for uncompressed formats an exact multiple of wBlockAlign (sample_frames * wBlockAlign). Derive it from the payload that was generated - never the other way round.
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.covers: every byte of waveformData[] or samples[] from the first sample byte to the last, i.e. lines 81/86/91/96/108; excludes the 8-byte 'data'+size header and excludes the pad byte at line 113
DATACHUNK.chunkSize.notes: Two invariants must hold simultaneously: chunkSize equals the number of payload bytes emitted, and chunkSize % wBlockAlign == 0 (line 78). The number of sample frames is what the top-level output_budget governs, so file size is controlled there and never by capping this field.

DATACHUNK.waveformData.tier_rationale: This is the opaque byte array the template falls back to when the sample shape is not one it understands (lines 77-82), and it is exactly the case where the .bt says nothing about the contents: for compressed wFormatTag values the bytes must be a real codec bitstream, and a decoder fed random bytes fails inside the codec before producing any audio.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.description: The audio payload of the data chunk, whose required internal structure is selected entirely by FORMATCHUNK.wFormatTag.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.codec: wFormatTag-dependent: raw little-endian PCM integers (tag 1), IEEE-754 little-endian floats (tag 3), ITU-T G.711 A-law 8-bit (tag 6), ITU-T G.711 mu-law 8-bit (tag 7), Microsoft ADPCM block stream (tag 2), DVI/IMA ADPCM block stream (tag 17), MPEG bitstream in RIFF (tags 80/85), GSM 6.10 (tag 49). For tags 1/3/6/7 there is no framing at all - only size agreement. Tags 2 and 17 are the real codec payloads.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.condition: reached when wBitsPerSample is not 8/16/32, or wBlockAlign == 0, or chunkSize % wBlockAlign != 0 (line 77-78); in a generator it is the payload for every wFormatTag whose samples the template does not type, notably 2, 6, 7, 17, 80 and 85
DATACHUNK.waveformData.must_produce: For tags 1/3/6/7: exactly chunkSize bytes, chunkSize an exact multiple of wBlockAlign, each sample stored in wBitsPerSample bits little-endian (8-bit PCM unsigned with bias 128, 16/24/32-bit PCM signed, float IEEE-754 LE, A-law/mu-law one byte per sample). For tag 17 (DVI/IMA ADPCM): a sequence of fixed-size blocks, each wBlockAlign bytes, each block being per channel a 4-byte header (2-byte signed 16-bit predictor sample, 1-byte step index, 1-byte reserved) followed by (wBlockAlign/wChannels - 4) bytes of 4-bit nibble-packed IMA deltas, decoding to wSamplesPerBlock samples per channel per block. For tag 2 (Microsoft ADPCM): blocks of wBlockAlign bytes each starting per channel with a 7-WORD header (delta, iCoef1 sample, iCoef2 sample) followed by 4-bit nibble-packed deltas decoded with the 25 coefficient pairs declared in the fmt extra bytes. For tag 85 (MPEG): whole MPEG frames as per the tag-85 RIFF layout.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.decoder_gate: For PCM/float/A-law/mu-law there is no internal framing to fail, so the gate is purely arithmetic: ffmpeg's wav demuxer sets the packet size from chunkSize and, if chunkSize % blockAlign != 0, the last partial frame is dropped and libsndfile reports a bad block align; if wBlockAlign disagrees with wChannels * wBitsPerSample, libsndfile returns SFE_WAV_BAD_BLOCKALIGN and decodes nothing. For tag 17 with random bytes, ffmpeg's adpcm_ima_wav decoder consumes nibbles against an out-of-range step index and clamps, emitting 'invalid ADPCM step index' style corruption and producing noise of the wrong length, so the block loop terminates early and the deeper resampling/output paths are never reached. For tag 2 with random bytes the coefficient-prediction arithmetic overflows the delta clamp and ffmpeg aborts the frame.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.generation_strategy: Choose wFormatTag, wChannels, wBitsPerSample and a free wBlockAlign first, then derive the payload from them. (1) PCM/float path (tags 1, 3): emit chunkSize = frames * wChannels * ceil(wBitsPerSample/8) bytes of little-endian samples of any amplitude; for 24-bit emit packed 3-byte two's-complement little-endian values. (2) A-law/mu-law path (tags 6, 7): emit chunkSize = frames * wChannels bytes of any G.711 codewords - all 256 byte values are legal codewords, so the contents are completely free. (3) DVI/IMA ADPCM path (tag 17), the simplest correct construction: emit ceil(chunkSize / wBlockAlign) blocks; in each block, per channel, write a 4-byte header with predictor = 0x0000, step index = 0x00 (clamped 0..88), reserved = 0x00, then fill the remaining (wBlockAlign/wChannels - 4) bytes with nibbles; an all-zero nibble run is a valid IMA delta stream (step 0, delta 0) and decodes to silence of exactly wSamplesPerBlock samples per channel, so wSamplesPerBlock must equal (wBlockAlign - 4*wChannels)*2/wChannels + 1 and the payload is derived from the free wBlockAlign/wChannels choice. (4) Microsoft ADPCM path (tag 2): emit 32 bytes of extra format data (coefficient count 7 plus the standard seven coefficient pairs 256,0 / 512,-256 / 0,0 / 192,64 / 240,0 / 460,-208 / 392,-232), then blocks whose per-channel 7-word header is delta=16, iCoef1 sample=0, iCoef2 sample=0 followed by zero nibbles. In every case the *bytes inside* the stream are free; only the block framing and the size agreement are pinned.
DATACHUNK.waveformData.notes: This is the highest-value entry in the file for WAV and the one the .bt gives no hint of: line 81 declares the payload as a raw byte run. Every field in derives_from stays free or derived-from-free - the payload is computed from them, never the reverse. Do not shrink wChannels, wBitsPerSample or wBlockAlign to fit a precomputed ADPCM block.

DATACHUNK.samples.tier_rationale: These are the four mutually exclusive declarations of the same audio payload (lines 86, 91, 96 and 108) that the template uses when the sample shape is one it understands; the array length is taken directly from chunkSize divided by the sample width, so the payload's byte count, element width and channel interleave must all agree with the fmt chunk or the decoder reads past or short of the audio.
DATACHUNK.samples.description: Typed sample array for the uncompressed paths: 8-bit, 16-bit or 32-bit mono samples, or an array of interleaved SAMPLES frames for the general case.
DATACHUNK.samples.field_type: uchar[chunkSize] | short[chunkSize/2] | int[chunkSize/4] | struct SAMPLES[chunkSize / wBlockAlign]
DATACHUNK.samples.codec: uncompressed PCM (WAVE_FORMAT_PCM = 1) or uncompressed IEEE-754 float (WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT = 3); no codec framing, no headers, no checksums
DATACHUNK.samples.condition: reached when wBitsPerSample is 8, 16 or 32 AND wBlockAlign != 0 AND chunkSize % wBlockAlign == 0 (lines 77-108)
DATACHUNK.samples.must_produce: Exactly chunkSize bytes of little-endian samples. Element width follows wBitsPerSample: 1 byte unsigned with bias 128 at 8 bits (lines 86 and 103), 2 bytes signed at 16 bits (lines 91 and 105), 4 bytes at 32 bits - signed integer for tag 1, IEEE-754 single precision for tag 3 (lines 96 and 107). Frame count is chunkSize / wBlockAlign and each frame holds wChannels consecutive samples (line 108). chunkSize must be an exact multiple of wBlockAlign.
DATACHUNK.samples.decoder_gate: There is no bitstream to be malformed, so the gate is arithmetic: if chunkSize % wBlockAlign != 0 the template itself takes the opaque fallback at line 81 and libsndfile/ffmpeg drop the trailing partial frame or report a bad block align; if wBlockAlign != wChannels * wBitsPerSample/8 libsndfile returns SFE_WAV_BAD_BLOCKALIGN and no samples are decoded; if chunkSize overruns the RIFF length declared in hsize the demuxer truncates the audio.
DATACHUNK.samples.generation_strategy: Pick wFormatTag (1 or 3), a free wChannels, a free dwSamplesPerSec, a wBitsPerSample from the tag's legal set, compute wBlockAlign = wChannels * wBitsPerSample/8, choose a free frame count bounded only by the top-level output_budget, emit frame_count * wBlockAlign bytes of little-endian samples of arbitrary amplitude, then write chunkSize = frame_count * wBlockAlign. The trivially correct payload is all-zero bytes (digital silence for 16/24/32-bit and float, DC 0 for 8-bit unsigned which is 0x80); any amplitude pattern including full-scale and clipping is equally valid, so keep the sample values themselves free.
DATACHUNK.samples.notes: One constraint entry covers all four declarations because they are the same field name in mutually exclusive branches: line 86 (uchar, mono 8-bit), line 91 (short, mono 16-bit), line 96 (int, mono 32-bit) and line 108 (struct SAMPLES array, multichannel). The sample VALUES are never constrained - amplitude diversity is free and costs nothing.

SAMPLES.channels.tier_rationale: These are raw sample values: every possible integer or float in the element width is a legal sample, no decoder inspects them for structure, and they are the only source of waveform diversity in the file - bounding them would produce files that are byte-identical apart from their headers.
SAMPLES.channels.description: The interleaved per-channel sample values of one audio frame, whose element type and array length are taken from wBitsPerSample and wChannels.
SAMPLES.channels.notes: The element TYPE is fixed by wBitsPerSample (lines 102-107: uchar at 8, short at 16, int at 32) and the array LENGTH by wChannels, but the values are free. Emit silence, DC, ramps, noise, full-scale and over-scale values across files - all are legal and all decode.

DATACHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment byte whose value no reader examines (line 112 gates only on chunkSize parity and file bounds), so it is unchecked padding and constraining it buys nothing.
DATACHUNK.padding.description: Single RIFF alignment byte emitted after the data chunk when its payload length is odd.
DATACHUNK.padding.notes: Presence and count are structural (one byte iff chunkSize is odd); the value is free. Count it in hsize, never in chunkSize.

FACTCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The dispatch switch at lines 548-551 instantiates FACTCHUNK only when the tag bytes read at line 535 are 'fact'; a wrong value sends those bytes to the unknown-chunk path instead.
FACTCHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying the fact chunk, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'fact'.
FACTCHUNK.chunkID.notes: The fact chunk is optional for PCM and IEEE float and required for compressed formats; see dependencies.

FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: It is a chunk length: the template does not bounds-check it here, but ffmpeg only reads the sample count when the fact chunk is exactly 4 bytes and libsndfile walks to the next chunk using this value, so a wrong size desynchronises the chunk stream and everything after the fact chunk is misparsed.
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the fact chunk payload, which is the single 4-byte uncompressed sample count.
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: 4 for the standard single-DWORD fact chunk. Some codecs extend it with additional data; if any extra bytes are emitted they must be counted here and the odd-alignment pad rule still applies.
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the uncompressedSize field at line 121 and any codec-specific extension bytes; excludes the 8-byte chunk header
FACTCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: The template omits an odd-size pad byte for this chunk, which is harmless at size 4 but would be a bug for an extended fact chunk; emit the pad whenever chunkSize is odd, per the RIFF rule.

FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.tier_rationale: It is a count field that must agree with the data chunk: ffmpeg sets the stream frame count and duration from it for non-PCM codecs and libsndfile uses it to sanity-check the frame count, so a value inconsistent with chunkSize/wBlockAlign yields a wrong duration and, in strict readers, a rejected stream. Deriving it costs no diversity because its inputs are free.
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.description: Number of samples (not bytes) the data chunk decodes to, used to recover the true length of a compressed stream.
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.algorithm: sample count, not byte count: for uncompressed formats DATACHUNK.chunkSize / wBlockAlign; for DVI/IMA ADPCM (tag 17) wSamplesPerBlock * (number of blocks); for Microsoft ADPCM (tag 2) the equivalent per-block sample count times the block count; for MPEG-in-WAV the number of decoded samples the frames yield
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.covers: no byte span - it describes the decoded length of the DATACHUNK payload
FACTCHUNK.uncompressedSize.notes: Compute it from the payload actually emitted. Do not use it to decide how much audio to emit - that is the output_budget's job.

CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier.tier_rationale: A cue identifier is arbitrary metadata that no decoder validates or branches on; pinning it would remove free variety for no depth at all.
CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier.description: Unique identifier of one cue point, referenced by SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point.
CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier.notes: Conventionally a small increasing integer starting at 1 and unique within the cue list, but uniqueness is not checked by any decoder. Referenced by name from SMPLCHUNK loops; keep them consistent if both chunks are emitted, which is free to arrange since both are unconstrained.

CUEPOINT.dwPosition.tier_rationale: An unchecked metadata offset: no conforming decoder uses cue positions to parse or decode audio, so any value yields a file that is still fully processed, and free offsets are pure diversity.
CUEPOINT.dwPosition.description: Sample position of the cue point, used to order cue points within the data.
CUEPOINT.dwPosition.notes: Spec-wise it is a sample index into the 'plst'/'data' sequence and cue points are conventionally kept in ascending order, but nothing validates it. Do not bound it to the actual sample count.

CUEPOINT.fccChunk.tier_rationale: It names the chunk the cue point refers to, but no decoder resolves or validates that reference, so an arbitrary FOURCC still produces a fully parsed file; treating it as a fixed 'data' would remove free variety.
CUEPOINT.fccChunk.description: FOURCC of the chunk containing the cue point, conventionally 'data' for waveform samples.
CUEPOINT.fccChunk.notes: The RIFF WAVE document defines it as the chunk ID of the chunk holding the referenced position - in practice 'data', and for playlist-referenced segments 'LIST'/'plst'/'slnt'. Recorded as Tier C because the choice is unvalidated and 'data' would only be a convention, not a gate. Emit 'data' most of the time and other FOURCCs occasionally.

CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.tier_rationale: A byte offset that only matters when the referenced chunk is a LIST segment; no decoder dereferences it during parsing, so a wrong value still yields a fully processed file.
CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.description: Byte offset of the start of the chunk containing the cue point, relative to the beginning of that chunk's data.
CUEPOINT.dwChunkStart.notes: Zero for cue points that reference the 'data' chunk directly. Left free on purpose: it is an offset field a careless author would pin, and pinning it removes variety without buying a single decoder branch.

CUEPOINT.dwBlockStart.tier_rationale: Same reasoning as dwChunkStart - an unvalidated byte offset that no decoder follows, so any value still produces a parseable file.
CUEPOINT.dwBlockStart.description: Byte offset of the start of the block containing the cue point, relative to the start of the containing chunk.
CUEPOINT.dwBlockStart.notes: Zero when the cue point addresses a sample in the 'data' chunk. No bound imposed.

CUEPOINT.dwSampleOffset.tier_rationale: The sample offset inside the addressed block; nothing in the parse path reads it, so a wrong value still yields a fully processed file, and free offsets give the cue list real variety.
CUEPOINT.dwSampleOffset.description: Sample offset of the cue point from the start of the addressed block.
CUEPOINT.dwSampleOffset.notes: Deliberately NOT bounded by the actual number of sample frames in the data chunk. Bounding it would couple the cue list to the audio length and shrink both; a decoder never checks the coupling.

CUECHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The dispatch switch at lines 552-555 instantiates CUECHUNK only when the tag bytes read at line 535 are 'cue ' (with the trailing space); a wrong value routes those bytes elsewhere and the cue list is never parsed.
CUECHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying the cue point list chunk, which must be 'cue ' - four bytes including the trailing space.
CUECHUNK.chunkID.notes: The trailing space is mandatory; 'cue' plus any other byte selects the unknown-chunk branch instead.

CUECHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: It is a chunk length: the template uses it to size the trailing unknown[] run at lines 142-143 and every reader advances to the next chunk by this value, so a wrong size misaligns the rest of the file.
CUECHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the cue chunk payload, excluding its own 8-byte header.
CUECHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: 4 (dwCuePoints) + 24 * dwCuePoints, since each CUEPOINT is six 4-byte fields (lines 126-131); plus any extra trailing bytes that are then carried in unknown[]
CUECHUNK.chunkSize.covers: dwCuePoints at line 138, the whole points[] array at line 139 and the unknown[] run at line 143
CUECHUNK.chunkSize.notes: The template omits an odd-size pad byte for the cue chunk (contrast lines 112-113, 153-154, 174-175, 185-186 and 508-509). RIFF still requires even chunk alignment, so emit the pad byte whenever chunkSize is odd and count it in hsize but not here.

CUECHUNK.dwCuePoints.tier_rationale: This is a repetition count that directly controls how many 24-byte CUEPOINT records are emitted, and every cue point is parsed identically regardless of its contents - so it is free variety. Total file size is bounded by the output_budget on the points[] repetition, never by capping this field.
CUECHUNK.dwCuePoints.description: Number of CUEPOINT records that follow in the points[] array.
CUECHUNK.dwCuePoints.notes: No minimum, no maximum and no 'sensible' set. Zero is legal and produces a 4-byte cue chunk, which is itself a distinct parse path worth emitting occasionally. Whatever value is chosen, CUECHUNK.chunkSize and the points[] length must be derived from it.

CUECHUNK.points.tier_rationale: The array length is read straight from dwCuePoints at line 139, so if the number of CUEPOINT records actually emitted disagrees with that count the template reads past or short of the chunk and every later chunk boundary is wrong.
CUECHUNK.points.description: Array of CUEPOINT records whose element count must equal dwCuePoints.
CUECHUNK.points.algorithm: element count: dwCuePoints; byte count: 24 * dwCuePoints (six 4-byte fields per CUEPOINT)
CUECHUNK.points.covers: the whole run of CUEPOINT records between dwCuePoints and the unknown[] tail at line 143
CUECHUNK.points.notes: Each element is exactly 24 bytes with no per-element length field, so the count is the only framing.

CUECHUNK.unknown.tier_rationale: Trailing filler the template consumes only to reach the declared chunk end (lines 142-143); its bytes are never inspected, so they are free.
CUECHUNK.unknown.description: Trailing bytes of the cue chunk beyond the dwCuePoints records.
CUECHUNK.unknown.notes: Contents free; its LENGTH is fixed at chunkSize - 4 - 24*dwCuePoints, which is normally zero. Emitting a few filler bytes here is a legal way to make chunkSize disagree with the record count and exercise the trailing-data path.

LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: A subchunk ID inside a LIST is a FOURCC drawn from a defined registry, and each recognised ID is a separate branch in the reader - ffmpeg matches every entry of its ff_riff_info_iff table (INAM, IART, ICOP, ISFT, ...) and libsndfile matches the adtl label/note IDs - so the legal set must be recorded in full rather than narrowed.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID.description: FOURCC identifying one subchunk of a LIST chunk: a RIFF INFO text tag, an associated-data-list tag, or any other registered list subchunk.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID.completeness_reason: LIST subchunk IDs are an open FOURCC namespace: the twenty-two I-prefix RIFF INFO tags listed are the complete set defined by Microsoft's RIFF INFO documentation, the five adtl tags (labl, note, ltxt, file, regn) are the complete associated-data-list set, and DISP/JUNK/plst/LIST round out the IDs seen in real WAVE files. Any other FOURCC is legal and simply reaches the 'unrecognised subchunk, skip by length' path, so the generator must treat arbitrary 4-byte values as legal too.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID.weighting_note: Favour the preferred IDs because each one is a separate lookup hit in ffmpeg's ff_riff_info_iff metadata table and therefore a distinct executed branch; still emit the rest of the legal set and occasional arbitrary FOURCCs, which take the default skip path. Case matters: ffmpeg's table is uppercase for INFO tags and lowercase for adtl tags.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID.notes: The template parses LIST subchunks generically (LISTSUBCHUNK, lines 147-155) and never inspects the ID, so this Tier B set comes from the RIFF specification and from the decoders being covered, not from the .bt.

LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: The LIST loop at lines 165-171 reads this value ahead of parsing with ReadUInt( FTell()+4 ) and only instantiates a LISTSUBCHUNK when the subchunk fits inside the parent chunkSize; a wrong value makes the loop take the unknown[] fallback at line 170 and every following subchunk is misaligned.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the subchunk payload held in listData, excluding the subchunk's own 8-byte header.
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: number of bytes written into listData (for a RIFF INFO string, the ASCII text length including its terminating NUL if one is written)
LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the entire listData run at line 150; excludes the 8-byte subchunk header and excludes the pad byte at line 154

lookahead_bound.purpose: reads the subchunk's declared size four bytes ahead of the subchunk header so the enclosing LIST loop can test at line 167 whether the subchunk fits within LISTCHUNK.chunkSize
lookahead_bound.effect_if_wrong: the test FTell() - pos + size <= chunkSize fails and the template falls back to uchar unknown[ chunkSize - (FTell() - pos) ] at line 170, consuming the rest of the LIST as opaque bytes - so no further LISTSUBCHUNK is parsed and the subchunk-level branches are never reached

LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: Two size invariants must hold at once: this value equals the listData length, and the sum of all subchunks (each 8 + chunkSize + pad) equals LISTCHUNK.chunkSize - 4.

LISTSUBCHUNK.listData.tier_rationale: This is free-form text or region metadata; the template copies it without inspection (line 150) and ffmpeg only length-bounds the string it stores as a metadata tag, so arbitrary bytes still parse and text content is a large source of file-to-file difference.
LISTSUBCHUNK.listData.description: The subchunk body: a NUL-terminated ASCII string for RIFF INFO text tags, a structured record for adtl tags, or arbitrary bytes for anything else.
LISTSUBCHUNK.listData.notes: Asking the mandated question 'what must be inside this opaque array?': for the INFO tags the RIFF specification calls for an ASCII string, NUL-terminated by convention, and for 'ltxt' a 20-byte header (sample length, purpose, country, language, dialect, code page) followed by text; but nothing in the container or in the readers enforces any of it. Contents stay free - only the LENGTH is fixed, at exactly LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize bytes. Vary the text freely: empty strings, no terminator, high-bit bytes, very long strings and unparseable binary all yield files the decoder still reads.

LISTSUBCHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment byte inside the LIST body whose value no reader checks (line 153 gates only on parity and file bounds), so it is unchecked padding.
LISTSUBCHUNK.padding.description: RIFF alignment byte emitted after a LIST subchunk whose payload length is odd.
LISTSUBCHUNK.padding.notes: Presence and count are structural: one byte iff LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize is odd. It is counted in LISTCHUNK.chunkSize (it lies inside the parent chunk body) but not in the subchunk's own chunkSize. Value is free.

LISTCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The dispatch switch at lines 560-563 instantiates LISTCHUNK only when the tag bytes read at line 535 are 'LIST'; a wrong value routes those bytes to the unknown-chunk path and the whole list-subchunk loop is never entered.
LISTCHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying a RIFF list chunk, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'LIST' in upper case.
LISTCHUNK.chunkID.notes: Upper case only - the template's string comparison is case-sensitive, as are the FOURCC comparisons in ffmpeg and libsndfile.

LISTCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: It is the loop bound for the subchunk scan at line 165 and the value the ReadUInt lookahead at line 166 is checked against at line 167; if it disagrees with the bytes actually present, the loop either stops early, leaving the tail to be reparsed as top-level chunks, or runs past the list into the next chunk.
LISTCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the LIST chunk payload: the 4-byte list type plus every nested subchunk with its header, payload and pad byte.
LISTCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: 4 (chunkType) + sum over each nested LISTSUBCHUNK of (8 + LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize + pad byte if odd) + the length of any unknown[] tail emitted at line 170
LISTCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: chunkType at line 161 and the entire while( FTell() - pos < chunkSize ) loop body at lines 165-171, where pos is captured at line 160; excludes the 8-byte chunk header and the LIST chunk's own pad byte at line 175
LISTCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: Build the LIST body first, measure it, then write this value. The loop condition at line 165 is a strict less-than against bytes consumed, so the body must total exactly chunkSize for the scan to terminate cleanly on a chunk boundary.

LISTCHUNK.chunkType.tier_rationale: The list type FOURCC selects which subchunk namespace the reader applies - ffmpeg keys its metadata handling on 'INFO' and its associated-data handling on 'adtl', libsndfile checks for 'adtl' when reading cue markers - so a small enumerated set matters, but the namespace is open and an unrecognised type only means the subchunks are skipped generically.
LISTCHUNK.chunkType.description: FOURCC naming the contents of the LIST chunk, immediately after its size field.
value_names: associated data list (labels, notes, labelled text regions, file references, regions)
LISTCHUNK.chunkType.completeness_reason: LIST types form an open FOURCC namespace defined per application. 'INFO' and 'adtl' are the two the RIFF WAVE documentation standardises for WAVE files and the two the decoders special-case; 'plst' is defined alongside the 'cue ' chunk for playlist segments. Any other FOURCC is syntactically legal and produces a list whose subchunks are read by length only.
LISTCHUNK.chunkType.weighting_note: Favour 'INFO' and 'adtl' because each triggers a distinct subchunk-ID registry and therefore extra executed branches in ffmpeg and libsndfile; still emit other FOURCCs, including empty lists, so the generic skip path is exercised.
LISTCHUNK.chunkType.notes: The template stores chunkType but never tests it (lines 160-171); the enumeration comes from the RIFF specification and from the readers being covered. Its value must stay consistent with the LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID namespace chosen for the body.

LISTCHUNK.unknown.tier_rationale: Leftover LIST bytes the template consumes only to reach the declared chunk end (line 170); their contents are never inspected, so they are free.
LISTCHUNK.unknown.description: Remaining bytes of the LIST chunk body that the subchunk scan did not consume.
LISTCHUNK.unknown.notes: Contents free; its LENGTH is whatever remains of the LIST body, normally zero. Deliberately emitting a trailing gap here is a legal way to make chunkSize disagree with the subchunk totals and reach the fallback path at line 170.

LISTCHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment byte whose value no reader checks (line 174 gates only on parity and file bounds), so it is unchecked padding.
LISTCHUNK.padding.description: RIFF alignment byte emitted after a LIST chunk whose payload length is odd.
LISTCHUNK.padding.notes: Presence and count are structural: one byte iff LISTCHUNK.chunkSize is odd. Counted in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize, never in chunkSize. Value free.

SMPLCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: The dispatch switch at lines 556-559 instantiates SMPLCHUNK only when the tag bytes read at line 535 are 'smpl'; a wrong value sends those bytes to the unknown-chunk path and the sampler chunk is never parsed.
SMPLCHUNK.chunkID.description: The FOURCC identifying the sampler chunk, which must be the four ASCII bytes 'smpl' in lower case.
SMPLCHUNK.chunkID.notes: Lower case 'smpl', not the 'SMPL' of the list-type namespace; the template's comparisons are case-sensitive.

SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: It is a chunk length: every reader advances to the next chunk by this value, and the pad test at line 508 uses it, so a size that disagrees with the sampler fields actually emitted misaligns every chunk that follows.
SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the sampler chunk payload, excluding its own 8-byte header.
SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: 36 (the nine 4-byte scalars Manufacturer through Sampler_Data at lines 496-504) + 24 * Num_Sample_Loops (each SMPLLOOPS is six 4-byte fields, lines 482-487) + Sampler_Data bytes of sampler-specific data if any are emitted
SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: Manufacturer through Sampler_Data at lines 496-504, the whole loops[] array at line 505 and any sampler-specific data bytes that Sampler_Data counts
SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: The template has no unknown[] tail for this chunk: after loops[] it goes straight to the pad test at line 508. So if Sampler_Data is non-zero the sampler-specific bytes must be emitted for the chunk to end on a boundary the template expects.

SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer.tier_rationale: The template's own display switch at lines 381-440 enumerates the MIDI Manufacturers Association codes and falls through to 'Unknown' for anything else, so this is a defined registry rather than a free value - but it is metadata only: no parser branches on it, so a wrong code never breaks the file.
SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer.description: MIDI Manufacturers Association code of the sampler the file was produced for, or 0 when unspecified.
SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer.completeness_reason: The 46 codes above are exactly those the template's display switch recognises (lines 383-440), but the MMA code space is an open registry and the switch has a default branch that simply prints 'Unknown', so any 32-bit value is legal. Values outside the list are not errors - they are unnamed.
SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer.weighting_note: Favour 0 plus the common synth manufacturers (Kawai, Roland, Korg, Yamaha, Kurzweil) since those hit a named display branch; still emit the full recognised list and occasional out-of-registry values, which take the default path. This field never changes what bytes are parsed.
SMPLCHUNK.Manufacturer.notes: Do not couple this to any other field - it is descriptive metadata only.

SMPLCHUNK.Product.tier_rationale: A free-form metadata DWORD identifying the sampler product; the template only prints it (lines 324-333) and no decoder branches on it, so any value still yields a fully processed file and free product codes add variety.
SMPLCHUNK.Product.description: Manufacturer-specific product identifier of the intended sampler.
SMPLCHUNK.Product.notes: Meaningless to any container-level reader; zero is the common default. Unbounded on purpose.

SMPLCHUNK.Sample_Period.tier_rationale: Sampler hint metadata in nanoseconds that the template only prints (lines 336-346); no decoder uses it to time anything, so any value yields a fully processed file, and free values here give sampler-metadata variety.
SMPLCHUNK.Sample_Period.description: Duration of one sample in nanoseconds, normally 1000000000 / dwSamplesPerSec.
SMPLCHUNK.Sample_Period.notes: The spec's conventional value is the reciprocal of dwSamplesPerSec expressed in nanoseconds, and 0 means 'use the format chunk value'. Deliberately left free: it is a hint no reader validates, so pinning it to 1000000000/dwSamplesPerSec would remove variety without adding a single decoder branch.

SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Unity_Note.tier_rationale: A MIDI note number hint that the template only prints (lines 312-321); nothing in the container or the decoders validates it, so any value still produces a fully processed file.
SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Unity_Note.description: MIDI note number at which the sample plays back at its natural pitch.
SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Unity_Note.notes: Spec convention is 0-127 with 60 = middle C, and 0xFFFFFFFF/0 is used for 'unspecified'; but the value is never checked against anything, so it is left unconstrained rather than bounded to a MIDI range.

SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Pitch_Fraction.tier_rationale: A fine-tune fraction the template only prints (lines 300-309); no reader validates it, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Pitch_Fraction.description: Fractional MIDI pitch offset above MIDI_Unity_Note, where 0 means exactly on note and 0x80000000 is half a semitone above.
SMPLCHUNK.MIDI_Pitch_Fraction.notes: Full 32-bit range is legal; 0 is the usual value. Left free because it is never used to compute a byte offset or a buffer length.

SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE.tier_rationale: This one has a genuine enumerated meaning: the template's display switch at lines 357-365 recognises exactly 0, 24, 25, 29 and 30, and SMPTE frame-rate codes are a closed registry, so the value set should be recorded. It is not Tier A because no parser gates on it - the switch's default branch still prints 'unknown' and parsing continues.
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE.description: SMPTE time-code format the sample was synchronised to, or 0 when there is no SMPTE offset.
value_names: 30 frames per second with frame dropping (30 drop)
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE.completeness_reason: The smpl chunk specification defines exactly these five SMPTE format codes and the template's switch at lines 359-363 covers all of them; there is no reserved or extended range for this field.
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE.weighting_note: Favour 0 (no SMPTE offset, the overwhelmingly common case) and the 25/30 fps codes, which are what real recorder files carry; emit 24 and 29 for the remaining named branches. Values outside the set are still parseable - they simply display as 'unknown'.
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE.notes: If SMPTE is 0 then SMPTE_Offset should be 0 too, but that pairing is a convention, not a gate: nothing reads it.

SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE_Offset.tier_rationale: A synchronisation offset the template only prints (lines 288-297); no reader dereferences it into the audio, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE_Offset.description: SMPTE time-code offset for synchronisation, encoded as a packed time-code value.
SMPLCHUNK.SMPTE_Offset.notes: Spec layout is hours in bits 31-24, minutes 23-16, seconds 15-8 and frames 7-0 (the frame-rate code lives in SMPTE). The packing is a convention no reader validates, so it stays unconstrained.

SMPLCHUNK.Num_Sample_Loops.tier_rationale: This is a repetition count that directly controls how many 24-byte SMPLLOOPS records follow at line 505, and each loop record is parsed identically regardless of its contents - so it is free variety. The number of loops emitted is bounded by the top-level output_budget, never by a fixed span on this field.
SMPLCHUNK.Num_Sample_Loops.description: Number of sustain-loop records that follow in the loops[] array.
SMPLCHUNK.Num_Sample_Loops.notes: Zero is legal and common (a 36-byte sampler chunk), and so are several loops. Whatever is chosen, SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize and the loops[] length must be derived from it - that coupling is the constraint, not the range.

SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data.tier_rationale: It is a byte-count field that the template never consumes: line 504 reads the count and line 505 immediately parses loops[], so if sampler-specific bytes are present but not counted-and-skipped the chunk ends at the wrong offset and the pad test at line 508 plus the next chunk boundary are both wrong. Any reader that does honour this field walks past it by exactly this many bytes.
SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data.description: Byte count of sampler-specific data following the loop array, or 0 when there is none.
SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data.algorithm: byte count of the trailing sampler-specific run that is emitted after loops[]: normally 0. Must satisfy SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize == 36 + 24 * Num_Sample_Loops + Sampler_Data
SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data.covers: the trailing sampler-specific bytes after the loops[] array, if any are emitted
SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data.notes: The simplest correct choice is 0, which makes the chunk exactly 36 + 24*Num_Sample_Loops bytes. If a non-zero value is emitted, that many bytes must physically follow, because this template does not skip them.

SMPLCHUNK.loops.tier_rationale: The array length is read straight from Num_Sample_Loops at line 505, and since SMPLLOOPS has no per-element length field the count is the only framing - if the number of records emitted disagrees with it, the chunk ends at the wrong offset and every later chunk boundary is wrong.
SMPLCHUNK.loops.description: Array of SMPLLOOPS records whose element count must equal Num_Sample_Loops.
SMPLCHUNK.loops.algorithm: element count: Num_Sample_Loops; byte count: 24 * Num_Sample_Loops (six 4-byte fields per SMPLLOOPS, lines 482-487)
SMPLCHUNK.loops.covers: the whole run of SMPLLOOPS records between Sampler_Data and the chunk's pad byte at line 509
SMPLCHUNK.loops.notes: Each element is exactly 24 bytes. Emitting fewer or more records than Num_Sample_Loops is the classic way this chunk desynchronises the rest of the file.

SMPLCHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment byte whose value no reader checks (line 508 gates only on chunkSize parity and file bounds), so it is unchecked padding.
SMPLCHUNK.padding.description: RIFF alignment byte emitted after a sampler chunk whose payload length is odd.
SMPLCHUNK.padding.notes: Presence and count are structural: one byte iff SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize is odd. Counted in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize, never in chunkSize. Value free. Note that a well-formed smpl chunk is always a multiple of 4 bytes, so the odd case only arises if Sampler_Data carries an odd length.

SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point.tier_rationale: A cross-reference to a CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier; the template only prints it (lines 193-202) and no reader validates that the referenced cue exists, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point.description: Identifier of the cue point in the 'cue ' chunk that marks the loop start.
SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point.notes: By convention it equals the dwIdentifier of an existing CUEPOINT, and a sampler would use it to locate the loop start. Dangling references are not errors at the container level, so this stays free; emitting a 'cue ' chunk whose identifiers match is free variety, not a constraint.

SMPLLOOPS.Type.tier_rationale: The template's display switch at lines 454-474 recognises exactly 0, 1, 2 and 3, and the smpl specification defines these three playback modes plus a reserved range, so this is an enumerated registry value rather than a free one. It stays below Tier A because the switch has a default branch and no parser gates on the value.
SMPLLOOPS.Type.description: Playback mode of the sustain loop.
value_names: Loop: reserved for future standard types
SMPLLOOPS.Type.completeness_reason: The specification defines 0 = forward, 1 = ping pong (alternating direction), 2 = reverse, 3-31 = reserved for future standard types and 32-255 = reserved for sampler-specific extensions. Only 0, 1 and 2 have defined playback semantics and 3 is the reserved marker the template names explicitly at line 469; the default branch at lines 472-473 handles everything else, which is legal but unnamed.
SMPLLOOPS.Type.weighting_note: Favour 0 (forward), the overwhelmingly common case, then 1 and 2 which each take their own switch branch; emit 3 and out-of-range values occasionally for the reserved and default paths.
SMPLLOOPS.Type.notes: The loop type never changes how many bytes are read or where a chunk boundary falls, so it is not a structural constraint.

SMPLLOOPS.Start.tier_rationale: A loop-start offset the template only prints (lines 227-236); no reader seeks or bounds-checks it, so any value still yields a fully processed file and free offsets give the loop list real variety.
SMPLLOOPS.Start.description: Sample offset of the start of the loop region.
SMPLLOOPS.Start.notes: Conventionally a sample index with Start < End, but nothing validates the ordering or the range. Deliberately NOT bounded by the actual sample count of the data chunk: that coupling would shrink both the audio length and the loop values.

SMPLLOOPS.End.tier_rationale: A loop-end offset the template only prints (lines 239-248); no reader dereferences or bounds-checks it, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLLOOPS.End.description: Sample offset of the end of the loop region.
SMPLLOOPS.End.notes: Same reasoning as Start: the spec's Start < End convention is advisory. Left unconstrained so loop geometry stays a free diversity axis.

SMPLLOOPS.Fraction.tier_rationale: A fractional-sample offset the template only prints (lines 251-260); no reader applies it to a buffer length, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLLOOPS.Fraction.description: Fractional sample offset between Start and the true loop point, where 0x80000000 represents one half of a sample.
SMPLLOOPS.Fraction.notes: Full 32-bit range is legal; 0 is the usual value. Never used to compute a byte count, so unbounded.

SMPLLOOPS.Play_Count.tier_rationale: A playback-repeat count the template only prints, with an explicit special case at lines 213-216 where 0 means an infinite sustain loop; nothing gates on it, so any value still yields a fully processed file.
SMPLLOOPS.Play_Count.description: Number of times to play the loop, where 0 means loop indefinitely.
SMPLLOOPS.Play_Count.notes: 0 is the documented 'infinite sustain' value and is the most common in real files; any other 32-bit value is a finite repeat count. Both branches are display-only, so the field stays free.

UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.tier_rationale: This ID is defined by exclusion: the default branch of the switch at lines 564-571 is reached only for a FOURCC that is none of the six recognised chunk IDs, so the negative set must be recorded. It is not Tier A because violating it does not corrupt the file - it merely routes those bytes into a different, equally valid chunk parser.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.description: FOURCC of a chunk the template does not recognise, consumed by length only.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.forbidden_reason: Any of these six byte sequences matches an earlier case label of the switch at lines 538-563, so the bytes would be parsed by FORMATCHUNK, DATACHUNK, FACTCHUNK, CUECHUNK, SMPLCHUNK or LISTCHUNK instead of reaching the default branch at line 564.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.completeness_reason: The forbidden set is exactly the six case labels of the switch (lines 540, 544, 548, 552, 556, 560); every other possible 4-byte value falls through to the default branch at line 564, so the complement is fully characterised.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.weighting_note: Real WAVE files carry 'JUNK', 'bext' (BWF), 'ds64' (RF64), 'iXML' and 'pad ' as unknown chunks, so favour those for realism; also emit arbitrary and all-zero FOURCCs to exercise the same skip path with odd tag bytes.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkID.notes: Case-sensitive comparison, and the trailing space in 'fmt ' and 'cue ' matters: 'fmt' + any other byte is an unknown chunk.

UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize.tier_rationale: It is the skip length: line 182 reads exactly chunkSize bytes as unknownData and line 185 uses the same value to decide the pad byte, so if it disagrees with the bytes present the parser lands mid-chunk and everything after it is garbage.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize.description: Byte count of the unrecognised chunk's payload, which is skipped whole.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize.algorithm: byte count: number of payload bytes emitted for this chunk, whatever they are; excludes the 8-byte header and the pad byte at line 186
UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize.covers: the entire unknownData run at line 182

lookahead_bound.purpose: reads this same size four bytes ahead of the chunk header purely so the diagnostic at lines 567-568 can print the unknown chunk's tag and length
lookahead_bound.effect_if_wrong: none structurally - the printed number is cosmetic; the bytes actually consumed come from the chunkSize read at line 181 inside UNKNOWNCHUNK

UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize.notes: Because the contents are opaque, this field is the only thing that must be right: it decides where the next chunk header is read from.

UNKNOWNCHUNK.unknownData.tier_rationale: The template consumes this run without inspecting a single byte (line 182), and no reader interprets an unrecognised chunk, so the contents are entirely free - this is the one place in a WAV file where arbitrary binary data is guaranteed to be skipped safely.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.unknownData.description: The payload of the unrecognised chunk, skipped by length.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.unknownData.notes: Asking the mandated question 'what must be inside this opaque array?': nothing. There is no codec, no checksum, no terminator, no structure. Only the LENGTH is constrained, at exactly chunkSize bytes. This is the best place in the format to park filler, high-entropy bytes, NUL runs, nested look-alike chunk headers, or text metadata - all of it is skipped, which is itself a distinct decoder path worth covering.

UNKNOWNCHUNK.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment byte whose value no reader checks (line 185 gates only on chunkSize parity and file bounds), so it is unchecked padding.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.padding.description: RIFF alignment byte emitted after an unrecognised chunk whose payload length is odd.
UNKNOWNCHUNK.padding.notes: Presence and count are structural: one byte iff UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize is odd, and only if bytes remain (FTell() < FileSize()). Counted in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize, never in chunkSize. Value free.

then.requirement: The fmt chunk carries a WAVEFORMATEX tail: 2 bytes of wcbsize plus wcbsize bytes of codec-specific data. The template materialises this for tag 17 at lines 45-49 (wcbsize then wSamplesPerBlock, wcbsize == 2); tag 2 needs wcbsize == 32 followed by a coefficient count and 15 coefficient pairs; tag 65534 needs wcbsize == 22 followed by validBitsPerSample, channelMask and a 16-byte SubFormat GUID. For tags 1 and 3 no tail is emitted and chunkSize is exactly 16.

dependencies.derivation: FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize == 18 + FORMATCHUNK.wcbsize for tags that carry a tail; FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize == 16 otherwise
dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg allocates extradata of exactly cbSize bytes and libsndfile validates the fmt chunk length against it, so a tag that requires a tail and does not get one leaves the codec uninitialised, and a tail emitted for plain PCM desynchronises the chunk stream. The template only tests tag 17 explicitly; the tag 2 and tag 65534 cases come from the specification.

then.requirement: The data payload must be encoded in the codec named by wFormatTag: 1 = little-endian PCM integers of wBitsPerSample bits, 3 = little-endian IEEE-754 floats of wBitsPerSample bits, 6 = ITU-T G.711 A-law one byte per sample, 7 = ITU-T G.711 mu-law one byte per sample, 2 = Microsoft ADPCM blocks of wBlockAlign bytes each starting with a per-channel 7-WORD header, 17 = DVI/IMA ADPCM blocks of wBlockAlign bytes each starting with a per-channel 4-byte header, 80/85 = MPEG frames in RIFF, 49 = GSM 6.10 frames, 65534 = whatever SubFormat GUID says (which for PCM/float SubFormats reduces to tags 1/3).

dependencies.derivation: none - the tag selects the codec, the payload is then derived from the free geometry fields
dependencies.rationale: The template selects its sample representation from wBitsPerSample/wBlockAlign/channels only, but a real decoder selects the codec from wFormatTag first. Emitting raw PCM bytes under tag 17 makes ffmpeg's ADPCM decoder consume integers as nibbles and produce noise of the wrong length, so the deep decode paths are never reached. This is the single most important cross-field dependency in the format.

then.requirement: The legal wBitsPerSample values depend on the tag: 1 -> {8, 16, 24, 32}; 3 -> {32, 64}; 6 -> {8}; 7 -> {8}; 2 -> {4}; 17 -> {4}; 85 -> {0, 16} (bits per decoded PCM sample, not the MPEG payload width); 65534 -> whatever SubFormat and wValidBitsPerSample declare. The Tier B valid_values list on wBitsPerSample is the union of these per-tag sets and must not be treated as freely choosable per file.

dependencies.derivation: wBlockAlign follows from the chosen pair; for tags 2/17 wBlockAlign is free but must stay >= 4 * wChannels + wChannels so an ADPCM block holds its header plus at least one nibble byte per channel
dependencies.rationale: libsndfile rejects a WAV whose wBitsPerSample is unsupported for the declared tag (SFE_WAV_BAD_BITWIDTH / unsupported format) and ffmpeg sets the sample format from the tag plus bit-depth pair, so an impossible combination such as tag 3 with 8 bits yields no decoder at all.

then.requirement: For uncompressed tags wBlockAlign is derived, not chosen: wBlockAlign == wChannels * ceil(wBitsPerSample / 8). For tags 6 and 7 (G.711) that reduces to wBlockAlign == wChannels. For the compressed tags 2 and 17 wBlockAlign is a free geometry choice (the ADPCM block size) and wSamplesPerBlock is derived from it instead.

dependencies.derivation: uncompressed: wBlockAlign = wChannels * ceil(wBitsPerSample / 8); tag 17: wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign - 4 * wChannels) * 2 / wChannels + 1; tag 2: wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign / wChannels - 7) * 2 + 2
dependencies.rationale: libsndfile returns SFE_WAV_BAD_BLOCKALIGN when wBlockAlign disagrees with wChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 and decodes nothing; ffmpeg computes packet and frame sizes from blockAlign. Because wChannels and wBitsPerSample stay free, deriving wBlockAlign preserves all of that diversity while keeping the file valid.

then.requirement: wChannels == 0 makes the derived wBlockAlign 0, which the template rejects outright at line 78 (form.wBlockAlign == 0 forces the opaque waveformData fallback) and which leaves ffmpeg with no channel layout and libsndfile with a zero block align, so no samples can be decoded. Zero-channel files are a corruption case, not a diversity case: wChannels keeps its full Tier C range, and the generator avoids 0 unless a deliberately invalid file is requested.

dependencies.rationale: This is the one place where a free Tier C value makes a derived Tier A value illegal. The rule is stated on the derived field (forbidden_values 0) rather than by placing a numeric lower bound on wChannels, so the free axis keeps its full range and the prohibition stays explicit.

then.requirement: dwAvgBytesPerSec is derived and never chosen independently: dwAvgBytesPerSec == dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign for uncompressed tags, and == dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign / wSamplesPerBlock for ADPCM tags (equivalently the average bytes consumed per second of audio).

dependencies.derivation: dwAvgBytesPerSec = dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign (uncompressed); dwAvgBytesPerSec = dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign / wSamplesPerBlock (tags 2 and 17)
dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg's wav demuxer uses dwAvgBytesPerSec for the reported stream bit rate and for buffer sizing on compressed tags, and libsndfile cross-checks it against the block align when validating the header; a value inconsistent with the geometry yields a wrong reported duration and, in strict readers, a rejected stream. dwSamplesPerSec itself stays a free Tier C axis, so nothing is lost by deriving this field.

then.requirement: A 'fmt ' chunk must have been emitted earlier in the file. The template holds a file-scope flag haveValidFormat (declared line 21, set line 52) and at lines 70-74 emits Warning( "File contains no valid WAVE format chunk." ) and return -1 when a data chunk is reached without one, abandoning the rest of the parse.

dependencies.rationale: Every decoder reads the sample geometry from the fmt chunk before touching the data chunk: ffmpeg's wav_read_header scans for 'fmt ' first and returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA if the data chunk arrives without it, and libsndfile does the same. The chunk ORDER is therefore a hard structural rule, not a stylistic one - it is the only place in this format where a sequence matters.

then.requirement: Emit exactly one alignment byte after the chunk payload when chunkSize is odd and none when it is even. The template encodes this at lines 112-113, 59-60, 153-154, 174-175, 508-509 and 185-186 as if( (chunkSize & 1) && (FTell() < FileSize()) ) uchar padding;. The pad byte counts towards WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize but never towards the chunk's own chunkSize. FACTCHUNK and CUECHUNK have no pad rule in this template, but RIFF still requires even alignment for them too.

dependencies.rationale: RIFF requires every chunk to start on an even byte offset. Omitting the pad after an odd-sized chunk makes every subsequent chunk header start one byte early, so its FOURCC is read from the wrong offset and the whole remainder of the file becomes unrecognised chunks. The byte's VALUE is never checked, only its presence.

then.requirement: When chunkSize is not an exact multiple of wBlockAlign (or wBitsPerSample is not 8/16/32, or wBlockAlign is 0) the template abandons typed sample parsing at lines 77-82 and reads the payload as an opaque byte run instead. A generator that wants the sample arrays parsed must emit chunkSize == frame_count * wBlockAlign exactly.

dependencies.derivation: frame_count = chunkSize / wBlockAlign; choose frame_count freely (bounded by output_budget) and derive chunkSize from it
dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg's wav demuxer rounds the packet size down to a whole number of block aligns and drops the trailing partial frame; libsndfile reports a bad block align. Deriving chunkSize from a free frame count keeps the audio length diverse while guaranteeing the multiple-of-block-align invariant.

then.requirement: hsize must equal FileSize() - 8, i.e. 4 bytes of riffType plus the sum over every top-level chunk of (8-byte header + chunkSize + pad byte). Compute it after all chunks exist. Do not count pad bytes inside chunkSize and do not count the 8-byte RIFF header itself.

dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg derives riff_end from this field and stops scanning chunks there, so an under-declared hsize hides the data chunk entirely and an over-declared one makes the demuxer read past EOF and warn; libsndfile truncates or errors on a mismatch. This is the outermost size agreement and it subsumes every per-chunk chunkSize.

then.requirement: Each repetition count must equal the number of fixed-width records actually emitted: CUECHUNK.points has dwCuePoints elements of 24 bytes each (line 139), and SMPLCHUNK.loops has Num_Sample_Loops elements of 24 bytes each (line 505). Neither record type carries its own length, so the count is the only framing. SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data likewise counts trailing sampler-specific bytes that must physically follow, because the template does not skip them.

dependencies.derivation: CUECHUNK.chunkSize = 4 + 24 * dwCuePoints (+ any unknown tail); SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize = 36 + 24 * Num_Sample_Loops + Sampler_Data
dependencies.rationale: Emitting fewer records than the count declares makes the reader run past the chunk into the next chunk's header; emitting more leaves the surplus to be misread as a chunk tag. The counts themselves stay free Tier C repetition axes, so this coupling costs no diversity - it is the array length that must follow the count, never the reverse.

then.requirement: The LIST body must total exactly chunkSize bytes: 4 for chunkType plus, per subchunk, 8 + LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize + pad byte. The scan loop condition at line 165 is a strict less-than against bytes consumed, and the lookahead at lines 166-167 reads the next subchunk's size four bytes ahead and only instantiates a LISTSUBCHUNK while FTell() - pos + size <= chunkSize; otherwise the remainder is consumed as opaque bytes at line 170.

dependencies.rationale: This is the nested-container size agreement: a subchunk that overruns the declared LIST length is not parsed as a subchunk at all, so none of the INFO/adtl branches are reached, and a LIST that under-declares its body leaks the surplus bytes into the top-level chunk loop where they are read as bogus chunk headers.
