then.requirement: A 'fact' chunk should be emitted for compressed formats, carrying the decoded sample count. For uncompressed tags 1 and 3 it is optional and normally absent; when present its uncompressedSize must still equal DATACHUNK.chunkSize / wBlockAlign.

evidence.snippet: // Stores the size of the wave after decompression

dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg's wav demuxer reads the fact chunk sample count for compressed streams to establish duration and frame count, and falls back to estimating from the byte rate when it is absent; libsndfile uses it for the same purpose. Omitting it does not break decoding but yields a wrong or unknown duration, so it is recorded as should-emit (hard: false) rather than must-emit.

then.requirement: The sample element width and signedness follow wBitsPerSample: 8 -> one unsigned byte with bias 128 (lines 86 and 103), 16 -> one signed 16-bit little-endian word (lines 91 and 105), 24 -> one packed 3-byte little-endian two's-complement integer, 32 -> one 32-bit little-endian value, a signed integer for tag 1 and IEEE-754 single precision for tag 3 (lines 96 and 107). Each frame holds wChannels consecutive elements and frames are interleaved, never planar.

dependencies.derivation: bytes per frame = wChannels * ceil(wBitsPerSample / 8) = wBlockAlign; frames = chunkSize / wBlockAlign
dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg maps wBitsPerSample to an AVSampleFormat (U8 at 8, S16 at 16, S24 for packed 24, S32/F32 at 32) and reads the payload with that width; reading 16-bit samples as 8-bit halves the frame count and desynchronises every later frame. The sample VALUES remain completely free.

then.requirement: Subchunk IDs should be drawn from the namespace named by chunkType: 'INFO' -> the twenty-two I-prefix RIFF INFO tags; 'adtl' -> labl, note, ltxt, file, regn. A mismatch is still parseable - readers match subchunk IDs against their own tables regardless of the enclosing list type - but the metadata is then dropped.

dependencies.rationale: ffmpeg's ff_riff_info_iff metadata table and libsndfile's adtl handling key off the subchunk ID; the list type only tells a human reader which table applies. Recorded as soft (hard: false) because violating it loses metadata rather than breaking the parse.

then.requirement: When both chunks are emitted, each SMPLLOOPS.Cue_Point should equal the dwIdentifier of some CUEPOINT in the 'cue ' chunk. Both fields are Tier C, so this is free to arrange and nothing breaks if it is ignored.

dependencies.rationale: Sampler applications resolve loop start positions through the cue list; container-level readers do not. Recorded as soft (hard: false) so the generator can honour it for realistic files without treating a dangling reference as an error.

structure.byte_order_note: Every integer in the format is a little-endian fixed-width field. FOURCC tags are four ASCII bytes in file order, not integers, so 'RIFF' is 0x52 0x49 0x46 0x46 on disk. There is no big-endian variant and no byte-order marker.
structure.container_model: RIFF form: one 12-byte header (groupID, hsize, riffType) followed by a flat sequence of TLV chunks until end of file. One chunk type (LIST) is itself a nested container with the same TLV rule inside it.

file_layout.detail: 'RIFF' + hsize + 'WAVE'. hsize is written last, once every following byte exists (WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize, line 30).

Must be the first chunk after the header. 16 bytes of payload for tags 1 and 3; 20 for tag 17 (wcbsize + wSamplesPerBlock); 50 for tag 2 (wcbsize 32 + 2 + 30 bytes of coefficients); 40 for tag 65534 (wcbsize 22 + the WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE tail).

Any of 'fact', 'LIST' (INFO or adtl), 'cue ', 'smpl', or unrecognised chunks such as 'JUNK'/'bext'. Order among these is free; the only ordering rule in the format is that 'fmt ' precedes the sample parse.
Required. Payload is derived from the geometry chosen in the fmt chunk (DATACHUNK.samples / DATACHUNK.waveformData).
'cue ', 'smpl', 'LIST', 'fact' and unknown chunks may also appear after the data chunk; the chunk loop at lines 532-573 accepts them anywhere.
hsize = FileSize() - 8 = 4 + SUM(8 + chunkSize + (chunkSize & 1)) over every top-level chunk.

mandatory_chunks.position: first chunk after the 12-byte RIFF header
mandatory_chunks.why: The template's haveValidFormat gate at lines 70-74 returns -1 on reaching a data chunk without it; ffmpeg and libsndfile refuse the file outright.
Without a data chunk there is no audio to decode; ffmpeg returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA from wav_read_header when no data chunk was found.

optional_chunks.why: Carries the decoded sample count; expected for compressed tags, normally absent for PCM/float.
Cue point list; referenced by name from 'smpl' loops.
Sampler metadata and sustain loops; ignored by ffmpeg's audio path.
Nested metadata container (INFO tags, adtl labels/notes/regions). Multiple LIST chunks with different types are legal.
Unrecognised chunks are skipped by length (lines 564-571), so 'JUNK', 'bext', 'ds64', 'iXML' and arbitrary tags are all legal.

chunk_scan_rule.description: while( !FEof() ): read 4 tag bytes, dispatch on them, and let each chunk's own chunkSize decide where the next tag is read from.
chunk_scan_rule.implication: There is no chunk-count field and no index. The scan ends at end of file, so every chunkSize in the file must be self-consistent or the scan desynchronises and the remaining bytes are consumed as unrecognised chunks.

termination.detail: No terminator chunk, no sentinel, no reserved trailer and no CRC anywhere in the format. The file simply ends after the last chunk and its pad byte. hsize is the only declared length and equals FileSize() - 8.
termination.notes: Because termination is EOF, a truncated file is detected only by a chunk that overruns hsize - which is exactly what makes the size-agreement dependencies the dominant correctness property of this format.

repeating_structures.element: one RIFF chunk: 4-byte tag + 4-byte chunkSize + chunkSize payload bytes + pad byte if odd
repeating_structures.count_field: none - the loop runs to end of file

output_budget.rationale: The two mandatory chunks ('fmt ' and 'data') are the floor; the ceiling exists only to keep generated files small and is not a format limit. Within the budget, vary which optional chunks appear and in what order - chunk composition is a primary diversity axis, so spend the budget on distinct compositions rather than on many copies of the same one.

repeating_structures.notes: Duplicating 'fmt ' or 'data' is legal at the container level but a decoder takes its stream parameters from the last one read; treat repeats of mandatory chunks as an intentional corruption case, not part of the normal budget.

repeating_structures.element: one audio frame: wBlockAlign bytes (wChannels interleaved samples), or for ADPCM one wBlockAlign-byte codec block

output_budget.rationale: One frame is the smallest payload that satisfies chunkSize % wBlockAlign == 0; 96000 frames is two seconds at 48 kHz and keeps files under a few megabytes even at 32-bit stereo. The default of 4800 frames is 0.1 s at 48 kHz - small enough to fuzz at high throughput while still exercising buffering, ADPCM block looping and duration reporting. This budget is the ONLY thing that bounds audio length: never cap DATACHUNK.chunkSize or wBlockAlign to shrink a file.

repeating_structures.notes: frame_count is derived from chunkSize and wBlockAlign; the free choice is frame_count, and chunkSize is then frame_count * wBlockAlign. For ADPCM the element count is block_count and each block decodes to wSamplesPerBlock samples per channel.

repeating_structures.element: one interleaved sample value inside a frame

output_budget.rationale: This loop is not independently budgeted - its length is exactly wChannels, a free Tier C axis. The ceiling of 18 covers 5.1 plus rear and height channels with headroom, which keeps wBlockAlign and frame size realistic without narrowing the field; a generator may exceed it at the cost of very large frames. Values 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 cover the layouts real decoders handle best.

repeating_structures.notes: wChannels == 0 is excluded by the zero_channels_forces_invalid_blockalign dependency, not by this budget.

output_budget.rationale: Zero is legal and produces a 4-byte cue chunk worth emitting occasionally; the ceiling exists only to bound file size at 24 bytes per record. Vary the count across files - dwCuePoints is a free Tier C axis and every distinct count is a distinct parse length.

repeating_structures.notes: CUECHUNK.chunkSize must be derived as 4 + 24 * dwCuePoints (plus any unknown tail).

output_budget.rationale: Zero loops gives a bare 36-byte sampler chunk; one sustain loop is the realistic common case; the ceiling only bounds file size at 24 bytes per record. Free variation of the count exercises different loop-record counts without touching any derived size field except SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize.

repeating_structures.notes: SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize must be derived as 36 + 24 * Num_Sample_Loops + Sampler_Data.

repeating_structures.element: one LISTSUBCHUNK: 4-byte ID + 4-byte chunkSize + chunkSize payload bytes + pad byte if odd
repeating_structures.count_field: none - the loop is bounded by LISTCHUNK.chunkSize

output_budget.rationale: An empty LIST (chunkSize 4, just the type) is legal and is its own parse path; 16 subchunks bounds file size while still letting each LIST carry a varied tag mix. Spend the budget on distinct subchunk IDs from the Tier B set, which is where the extra reader branches live.

repeating_structures.notes: LISTCHUNK.chunkSize is derived from the subchunks actually emitted (4 + SUM(8 + chunkSize + pad)), and each subchunk's own chunkSize from its listData length.

structure.output_budget_note: Every repeating structure above carries an explicit output_budget, including the two whose element count is derived from a declared field (points[] from dwCuePoints, loops[] from Num_Sample_Loops) and the two bounded by EOF or by a parent chunkSize. Budgets bound the number of elements EMITTED so generated files stay small; they never bound a format field's legal value range, and a Tier C count field must not be narrowed to satisfy one.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: This is the format's single deepest axis: each tag selects a different codec, a different legal wBitsPerSample set, a different fmt-chunk tail, a different payload encoding and a different decoder in the target. Sweeping the full Tier B registry multiplies the code reached per file far more than any numeric axis does.
diversity_axes.budget: one tag per file; distribute files across the sweep rather than defaulting to PCM
diversity_axes.interaction: Drives wBitsPerSample's legal set, wBlockAlign's derivation rule, the presence of the fmt tail, the data payload encoding and whether a 'fact' chunk is expected. Never adjust those to fit a precomputed payload - choose the tag first and derive everything downstream.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Channel count changes wBlockAlign, the SAMPLES.channels[] element count, ffmpeg's channel-layout handling and every per-frame byte offset. Odd and unusual counts (3, 5, 7) reach layout paths that 1 and 2 never do, and 16/18-channel files exercise the multi-channel buffer paths.
diversity_axes.budget: unbounded by any spec field; bounded in practice by the SAMPLES.channels[] output_budget (max 18) to keep frames a sane size
diversity_axes.interaction: wChannels == 0 is forbidden because it forces wBlockAlign == 0, which the template rejects at line 78 and which leaves decoders with no channel layout. Every other value in the 16-bit unsigned range is free.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: The sample rate drives resampler selection, duration computation, buffer sizing and rate-conversion paths in every decoder, and unusual rates (1 Hz, 3 Hz, very high rates) reach the validation and resampling code that common rates skip.
diversity_axes.budget: unbounded; the field is a free 32-bit unsigned axis
diversity_axes.interaction: dwAvgBytesPerSec is derived from it, so changing the rate never invalidates the header. It has no effect on wBlockAlign or on the payload byte count, which is exactly why it can stay completely free.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Bit depth selects the sample element type and the AVSampleFormat the decoder instantiates (U8, S16, S24, S32, FLT, DBL) and therefore a distinct conversion path per depth. 24-bit packed PCM and 64-bit float in particular reach code that 8/16 never do.
diversity_axes.budget: one value per file, drawn from the legal set of the chosen wFormatTag
diversity_axes.interaction: Constrained only by the wBitsPerSample_legal_set_selected_by_wFormatTag dependency - the full Tier B list is the union across tags and must never be sampled independently of wFormatTag. wBlockAlign is derived from it, so no numeric span is needed or wanted here.

diversity_axes.derivation: uncompressed tags (1, 3, 6, 7, 65534): wBlockAlign = wChannels * ceil(wBitsPerSample / 8). Compressed tags (2, 17): wBlockAlign is a free geometry choice (the codec block size) and wSamplesPerBlock is derived from it instead.
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: It carries diversity indirectly: for uncompressed tags it inherits every wChannels and wBitsPerSample combination automatically, and for ADPCM tags it is itself a free axis that determines block size and therefore how many blocks a given payload splits into.
diversity_axes.budget: never chosen independently for uncompressed tags; for tags 2/17 keep it a free multiple that satisfies wBlockAlign >= wChannels * (4 + 1) for tag 17 and >= wChannels * 7 words for tag 2
diversity_axes.interaction: Listed as an axis because it appears in DATACHUNK.samples.derives_from and DATACHUNK.waveformData.derives_from. 'must_remain_unconstrained' here means it must never be pinned to a constant to suit a precomputed payload - it is computed from the free fields, so the payload is always derived from the geometry, never the reverse.

diversity_axes.derivation: dwAvgBytesPerSec = dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign (uncompressed); = dwSamplesPerSec * wBlockAlign / wSamplesPerBlock (tags 2, 17)
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Inherits the full cross-product of the free dwSamplesPerSec and wChannels/wBitsPerSample axes, so it sweeps hundreds of distinct values without being constrained itself.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - purely derived
diversity_axes.interaction: Must be recomputed whenever any input changes; never patched to match a payload.

diversity_axes.derivation: tag 17: wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign - 4 * wChannels) * 2 / wChannels + 1. tag 2: wSamplesPerBlock = (wBlockAlign / wChannels - 7) * 2 + 2
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Appears in DATACHUNK.waveformData.derives_from: it is the per-block decode length the ADPCM payload must actually produce, so it has to be computed from the free wBlockAlign/wChannels choice.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - present only for tags 2 and 17
diversity_axes.interaction: The classic inversion trap: never fix wSamplesPerBlock first and then bend wBlockAlign or wChannels to match it.

diversity_axes.derivation: byte count of the codec tail actually emitted: 2 for tag 17, 32 for tag 2, 22 for tag 65534, absent for tags 1/3
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Appears in DATACHUNK.waveformData.derives_from because the tag-2 coefficient table it declares is part of the payload contract; it must describe the bytes emitted rather than a fixed guess.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - fixed by the chosen wFormatTag
diversity_axes.interaction: FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize == 18 + wcbsize must hold, and FORMATCHUNK.unknown's length is whatever remains of the chunk after it.

diversity_axes.derivation: chunkSize = frame_count * wBlockAlign, where frame_count is the free choice bounded only by the DATACHUNK.samples[]/waveformData[] output_budget (min 1, max 96000, default 4800 frames)
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: It is the axis through which audio length varies: payload sizes from one block up to several megabytes all reach different buffering, packetisation and duration paths in the decoder. It appears in both payload entries' derives_from.
diversity_axes.budget: governed by the frame-count output_budget above, never by a numeric span on this field
diversity_axes.interaction: Must stay an exact multiple of wBlockAlign (line 78) and must equal the number of payload bytes emitted; both invariants are derived from the free frame count, so nothing is lost.

diversity_axes.derivation: hsize = FileSize() - 8 = 4 + SUM over top-level chunks of (8 + chunkSize + (chunkSize & 1))
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: It varies automatically with chunk composition and payload size, so a generator that sweeps chunk sets and audio lengths gets a wide range of RIFF lengths for free - including the odd/even pad cases.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - purely derived, computed after every chunk exists
diversity_axes.interaction: Subsumes every per-chunk chunkSize; if any of them changes, this must be recomputed rather than patched.

diversity_axes.derivation: = frame_count for uncompressed tags (chunkSize / wBlockAlign); = wSamplesPerBlock * block_count for tags 2 and 17
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: It tracks the audio-length axis into the compressed-codec duration path, which is where ffmpeg uses it to size the stream - so compressed files inherit the same length diversity as PCM files.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - purely derived
diversity_axes.interaction: Emit the fact chunk only for the tags that expect it, but always derive this value from the payload actually generated.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Sample values are the only free content inside the audio payload and they cost nothing: every amplitude pattern decodes identically as far as the container is concerned, yet different patterns reach different code in converters, dithering, clamping and float-to-int paths. This is also where the DATACHUNK.samples and DATACHUNK.waveformData entries point their derives_from.
diversity_axes.budget: element count per frame is wChannels (see its output_budget); values are unbounded
diversity_axes.interaction: Element TYPE is fixed by wBitsPerSample and element COUNT by wChannels, but the values are never constrained. Do not narrow them to a 'sensible' audio range - silence, DC, noise and full-scale are all equally valid and each is a distinct decoder path.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: A free repetition count that changes how many 24-byte records are parsed and therefore how much of the cue-list loop is exercised; zero is its own distinct path (a 4-byte chunk).
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the CUECHUNK.points[] output_budget (min 0, max 64, default 4)
diversity_axes.interaction: CUECHUNK.chunkSize and the points[] length are derived from it - the count leads, the sizes follow.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Same role as dwCuePoints for the sampler chunk: a free count that varies how many loop records are read and how large the chunk is.
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the SMPLCHUNK.loops[] output_budget (min 0, max 32, default 1)
diversity_axes.interaction: SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize is derived as 36 + 24 * Num_Sample_Loops + Sampler_Data.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Each recognised ID is a separate hit in ffmpeg's ff_riff_info_iff metadata table or in libsndfile's adtl handling, so sweeping the Tier B registry multiplies executed branches inside the LIST path without touching any size field.
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the LISTCHUNK subchunk-scan output_budget (min 0, max 16, default 3 per LIST)
diversity_axes.interaction: Only its LENGTH-carrying partner LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize is constrained; the ID itself may be any four bytes, with unrecognised IDs taking the generic skip path.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Selects which subchunk namespace the reader applies, and therefore which metadata-handling branches run inside the LIST.
diversity_axes.budget: one per LIST chunk; multiple LIST chunks with different types are legal
diversity_axes.interaction: Soft consistency with LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkID (list_type_selects_subchunk_namespace); violating it drops metadata but never breaks the parse.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Every unrecognised tag exercises the default skip branch at lines 564-571 with different bytes, including pathological tags (NUL bytes, non-ASCII) that stress the diagnostic Printf and the length-based skip.
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the top-level chunk-sequence output_budget (min 2, max 8, default 4)
diversity_axes.interaction: Must not equal any of the six recognised FOURCCs, or the bytes are parsed by a different chunk struct instead.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Free-form metadata text is a large source of file-to-file difference and reaches the string-length, charset-conversion and tag-storage paths in ffmpeg's metadata handling. Only its LENGTH is constrained (== LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize).
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the LISTCHUNK subchunk-scan output_budget through the number and size of subchunks
diversity_axes.interaction: Changing the text length changes LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize, which changes LISTCHUNK.chunkSize and WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize - all derived, so the text stays free.

sweep: a copy of the fmt chunk
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: The one place in the format where arbitrary binary data is guaranteed to be skipped safely, so it is the cheapest way to vary file size, alignment parity and skip-loop behaviour without risking a decode failure.
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the top-level chunk-sequence output_budget through the number of unknown chunks
diversity_axes.interaction: Only the LENGTH is constrained (== UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize); an odd length is useful because it forces the alignment pad byte.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Pad byte VALUES are never inspected, so they are free content; what matters is their PRESENCE, which is a hard structural rule tied to chunkSize parity. Varying the value adds byte-level difference at zero risk.
diversity_axes.budget: 0 or 1 byte per chunk, decided by parity
diversity_axes.interaction: Counted in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize but never in the owning chunk's chunkSize.

diversity_axes.field: CUEPOINT.dwIdentifier / dwPosition / fccChunk / dwChunkStart / dwBlockStart / dwSampleOffset
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Six free 32-bit/FOURCC fields per cue point, none validated by any reader, so each combination is a distinct file that still parses fully. This is where cue-list diversity lives.
diversity_axes.budget: 24 bytes per record, bounded by the CUECHUNK.points[] output_budget
diversity_axes.interaction: Deliberately NOT bounded by the real sample count or by any offset arithmetic - the coupling to audio length is a convention only.

sweep: Manufacturer: 0 and the recognised MMA codes plus out-of-registry values
Start/End/Fraction: zero, ordered pairs, inverted pairs, out-of-range offsets
Product, Sample_Period, MIDI_Unity_Note, MIDI_Pitch_Fraction, SMPTE_Offset: full 32-bit range
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: The sampler chunk is pure metadata: every field is read and displayed but never used to seek, size a buffer or validate anything, so the whole 4-byte-per-field space is free diversity. Only the enumerated fields (Manufacturer, SMPTE, Type) have named branches worth hitting.
diversity_axes.budget: 36 bytes of scalars + 24 bytes per loop record, bounded by the SMPLCHUNK.loops[] output_budget
diversity_axes.interaction: SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data and SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize stay derived; if Sampler_Data is non-zero those bytes must physically exist because the template does not skip them.

sweep: fmt + data with a trailing LIST
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Chunk composition is a first-class axis: each optional chunk adds a struct, a dispatch branch and a size-agreement obligation, and the only ordering rule is that 'fmt ' precedes the sample parse. Distinct compositions reach more of every reader than any single numeric sweep.
diversity_axes.budget: bounded by the top-level chunk-sequence output_budget (min 2, max 8, default 4)
diversity_axes.interaction: Every composition changes WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize and each chunk's chunkSize - all derived, so composition is free to vary.

diversity_axes.field: FORMATCHUNK.chunkSize / FACTCHUNK.chunkSize / CUECHUNK.chunkSize / LISTCHUNK.chunkSize / LISTSUBCHUNK.chunkSize / SMPLCHUNK.chunkSize / UNKNOWNCHUNK.chunkSize
diversity_axes.derivation: each = the exact byte count of that chunk's own emitted payload, excluding the 8-byte chunk header and excluding the alignment pad byte
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: These are the length-agreement obligations that give a RIFF file its depth: each one inherits, for free, the diversity of whatever free content or free count it wraps, so sweeping payload content and repetition counts automatically sweeps every declared length. They are listed as a group because they are one identical rule applied at seven sites, and because WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.depends_on names each of them.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - purely derived; never chosen, never patched after the fact
diversity_axes.interaction: Computed after the payload exists; each feeds WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize. A mismatch between a declared chunkSize and the bytes actually emitted is the single most detectable fault in the format, so these must never be treated as free values.

diversity_axes.field: DATACHUNK.samples / DATACHUNK.waveformData / CUECHUNK.points / SMPLCHUNK.loops / FORMATCHUNK.unknown / LISTCHUNK.unknown / SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data / LISTSUBCHUNK.padding
diversity_axes.derivation: byte length is fixed by the owning count or size field: samples/waveformData by DATACHUNK.chunkSize, points by dwCuePoints, loops by Num_Sample_Loops, unknown by the bytes remaining in the parent chunk, Sampler_Data by SMPLCHUNK.Sampler_Data, padding by chunkSize parity
diversity_axes.why_it_matters: These are the variable-length bodies of the format. Their LENGTHS are fully derived and must never be free, but their CONTENTS are the Tier C axes (sample values, metadata bytes, codec tail, filler) - which is why they appear here: named in depends_on/derives_from, and the place where the emitted-element output_budgets live.
diversity_axes.budget: each is bounded by the output_budget of the repeating structure that emits it (see structure.repeating_structures)
diversity_axes.interaction: For DATACHUNK.samples and DATACHUNK.waveformData only one is emitted, selected by whether wBitsPerSample/wFormatTag admits a typed element parse; both derive their length from DATACHUNK.chunkSize.

diversity_axes.why_it_matters: Listed for completeness only, because WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize.depends_on names it: it is a fixed magic value and contributes no diversity. The form type must be 'WAVE' or the file is not a WAV at all.
diversity_axes.budget: n/a - four constant bytes
diversity_axes.interaction: Its 4 bytes are counted in WAVRIFFHEADER.hsize, which is why hsize = FileSize() - 8 rather than FileSize() - 12.
